title: Hagestad & Settersten (2017): True or False
instructions: Use the reading to evaluate each statement's scope, direction, and strength, then choose True or False.

items.prompt: The authors question the separation between a public celebration of active aging and private discussions of limitations and finitude.
items.explanation: Keeping these discourses separate can distance gerontologists from the people they study and reproduce othering, ageism, and stigma.

items.prompt: The essay connects two autobiographical life histories with social theory rather than reporting a representative-sample experiment.
items.explanation: Personal experiences and theoretical concepts generate insights and questions; the authors do not estimate population effects from a representative experiment.

items.prompt: For Simmel and Schütz, the stranger is a complete insider who cannot question a group's taken-for-granted rules.
items.explanation: Nearness combined with distance can enable the stranger to ask how and why established social recipes work.

items.prompt: A co-biographer is only someone providing practical care now; shared memories across a life course are unimportant.
items.explanation: Co-biographers share longstanding experiences and help sustain the meanings and continuity of a person's life history.

items.prompt: GOH's cancer experience was also an interpersonal crisis that reorganized relationships and allowed the patient role to overshadow other identities.
items.explanation: Illness disrupted expected timetables and roles, and people moved between central and peripheral positions in her support convoy.

items.prompt: When RAS and Dan first adopted, the law recognized both men equally as adoptive parents from the outset.
items.explanation: RAS would be the legal adoptive parent, while Dan was designated a household member and kept outside the magistrate's chambers.

items.prompt: The essay treats marriage and family law as conditions of aging because legal recognition affects survivorship, medical involvement, and end-of-life decisions.
items.explanation: Legal recognition can support or restrict family roles and interdependent rights that matter in later life.

items.prompt: Interdependence refers only to the security of reliable relationships and therefore has nothing to do with risk or uncertainty.
items.explanation: One's circumstances also depend on other people's bodies and functioning. Relationships can provide continuity while introducing contingency and risk.

items.prompt: The authors argue that the histories of parents' and grandparents' cohorts can continue to shape lives through family relationships.
items.explanation: Historical experiences of significant others are carried forward through meanings, practices, and relationships, not only through one's own cohort membership.

items.prompt: Following the demographic transition, death became more evenly distributed across all ages and less closely associated with old age.
items.explanation: The essay describes longer, more predictable lives as linking finitude more strongly to old age.

items.prompt: The essay establishes that everyone who has been a social vanguard will adjust better to old age.
items.explanation: The authors ask whether strategies developed through hardship and stigma may help with aging. They do not establish an automatic resilience benefit.

items.prompt: The critique of active aging concerns restrictive either/or standards rather than a rejection of exercise or social participation themselves.
items.explanation: Labels such as active/passive or able/disabled can obscure the capacities and contributions that people retain despite bodily limitations.

items.prompt: The WHO perspective discussed in the essay understands disability partly through the relationship between individual capacity and environmental demands.
items.explanation: The authors use this relational perspective to challenge accounts based solely on an individual characteristic and to resist dichotomous labels.

items.prompt: The essay's gender contrasts claim that women's and men's biological natures remain fixed regardless of historical and policy conditions.
items.explanation: The discussion connects mortality, morbidity, family roles, and relationship opportunities to demographic and social change rather than offering a timeless biological explanation.

items.prompt: Anticipatory gerontology asks how current changes may shape the interpersonal worlds and options of future aging cohorts.
items.explanation: The task is to map emerging challenges and possibilities, not to predict every individual's future with certainty.
